column3: The Hebrew says God’s assembly and stands; BSB says divine assembly and presides.
The Hebrew pictures partiality as lifting the wicked’s faces.
The Hebrew directly commands judging and justifying the afflicted, where BSB says defend the cause and uphold rights.
The Hebrew’s final command leaves its object unstated; BSB supplies them.
The Hebrew has man in the singular and like one of the rulers; BSB has mortals and rulers in the plural.
The Hebrew makes You the active subject inheriting among all nations; BSB makes the nations Your inheritance.
